added_claims.speaker: Margrethe Vestager
added_claims.quote: if you look at how Europe approaches uh new technology we are tend to be more risk averse than in other parts
added_claims.claim: Europe regulates new technology more risk-aversely than other regions (e.g. requiring a human in the loop when municipalities use AI for welfare decisions, after a first scandal), a structural difference that shapes how fast tech products and AI uses reach the EU market.
added_claims.indicator: EU AI Act / DSA / DMA obligations
added_claims.testable: partly - product launch lags EU vs US

added_claims.speaker: Margrethe Vestager
added_claims.quote: do you improve competitiveness by regulating more uh no I don't think so
added_claims.claim: Big-tech threats to stop launching products in Europe because of regulation are taken as a signal that Europe must raise competitiveness; Vestager agrees more regulation does not improve competitiveness, except where tailored rules (e.g. a biotech act) shorten time to market.

added_claims.speaker: Interviewer
added_claims.quote: in banking it seems like one Bank needs to go bankrupt before it can be taken over by somebody else right like we saw in Switzerland credit s bank
added_claims.claim: In European banking, consolidation seems to happen only after failure (Credit Suisse had to collapse before UBS could buy it), leaving Europe without global champion banks; its largest bank ranks about 20th worldwide.
added_claims.indicator: European bank M&A; global bank size ranking
added_claims.testable: partly - count of cross-border EU bank mergers vs distressed takeovers

corrections.issue: Speaker mix and quote mismatch: 'the biggest European bank is number 20 worldwide, no champions' is the interviewer's statement; Vestager only says digitization challenges slowed European banks' recovery from the financial crisis versus the US. The attached quote is about gas supply, not banks.
corrections.fix: Vestager: European banks took longer than US banks to recover from the financial crisis, partly because they were challenged by digitization; the Commission has not assessed bank mergers she can recall. (The 'no champions, biggest bank about 20th' point is the interviewer's.)

completeness_estimate: 0.9 - policy interview with little systematic content; first reader captured almost all regulatory and industrial-policy ideas, missed Europe's risk-averse tech stance, the regulation/competitiveness exchange and the bank-consolidation-after-failure point.
